Straw poll: where do you buy the majority of your supplies: LHBS vs online
LHBS = local homebrew store. I appreciate there are options other than these two (supermarket, wholesale etc). If you don't fit either category let us know how you source your supplies

Let's see... I buy Equipment and Hops online, and yeast, grain and cleaning chemicals at my LHBS.

I buy whole hops in bulk yearly at harvest time, so that's online only. And for grain I buy bags and I haven't found a good online store for shipping 50+ lbs economically.
I usually buy equipment online and ingredients at the LHBS.
LHBS for ingredients except for bulk hop orders.
What is considered local. I sometimes have to drive nearly an hour to get to the shop, does that count? Granted main brew is one of the best shops local or online.

Interesting results, the majority of pollsters prefer the LHBS exclusively but about the same mix it up and do both.

My vote was exclusively online purchasing, the reason being that my LHBS isn't really up to much. I've found an online supplier that is cheaper to purchase from, even when I factor in the $10 shipping cost. It also turns up within 48 hours. I will only go to the LHBS for emergency purchases.

If you have a local home brew club and brewery why not go in with the brewery on yeasts and grains. Once a month when the brewery is doing their order we get a heads up and add ours. No shipping costs, no markups.

I'm pretty new to this, so I guess I can't say I've formed all my habits yet. So far, I've gotten most of my stuff online. The closest LHBS to me is half an hour drive without traffic, so it's easier to just get stuff shipped to my house, and if you factor in time, about the same price.
I buy pretty much everything online. If I want to add a certain yeast to the wort or need some equipment I'll hit up the LHBS.
I tend to buy online, my LHBS is extremely unfriendly and charge's way to much

Closest LHBS is 2-hours round trip drive, so unless I've planned ahead around a rare trip to that area, want to spend about 50% more and don't mind that it's covered in dust, LHBS.... meaning I do 99.999% of my buying online.

This is the closest I've lived to a LHBS in 15 years, before this I was 6~7 hours one way, and before that 3~4 hours one way. All of them have been the same crotchety/grumpy old men who seem annoyed someone is interrupting their alone time to look at their WAY past exp. liquid yeast, and years old grains/extracts. I really don't have a very good opinion of B&M homebrew stores... wish I could that wasn't the case, but I find more enthusiasm at the dentists office.
I am lucky. Three good to great shops within my usual prowl around town. Two within bike distance! For industrial plumbing and such: on-line.

I am lucky to be living in an area with a number of LHBS, so we try to spread out our purchases. One batch from one store, the next for another, choose online for another batch because I want something weird or don't have time to go to town before brew day, etc. The prices in the store are a bit higher, but not noticable so. The advice you can pick up in the store is worth much more than the price difference.
